title: Fall detection? I call BS.
text:
I have my watch for multiple reasons. One of those being fall detection because I am a professional equestrian rider. I have fallen no less than a dozen times since purchasing my first watch with “fall detection.”

Most recently I have an Apple Watch Series 9. I have come off of a horse 3 times (HARD) while having this watch and none of those  times was there an emergency alert. However, I have clapped my hands excitedly for someone and also had a mild roll off of my body ball while stretching where my watch has gone off. What gives on when this thing registers? Do I have to pound my fist on the ground (if I’m conscious) after I’ve come off to get a fall to register? WTH Apple?

I realize that an accelerometer is the primary source that registers to tell the watch to make an emergency call, but Apple really should rethink their “fall detection.” 

My mother had several falls as an elderly obese person that were not registered. This was the absolute primary reason for the purchase. We had backup emergency buttons as well. 

I’ve had numerous hard hits to the ground from horses or otherwise and there has been no “fall” detected. 

I am well aware that this is not the end all be all in fall detection, but it fails nine times out of 10 in actual fall scenarios versus false positives for ridiculous everyday movements. 

Come on Apple, I know you can do better. I am absolutely happy to be a test subject for your fall detection upgrades since I continue to have many  instances in which it SHOULD register. 

My only saving grace is that, THANKFULLY,  the times I have come off, my cellular has worked. That is also a very sketchy issue. Cellular on the Apple Watch works at its own convenience.

And, if I don’t check in, my emergency contacts will get a text message from the app to inform them I’ve gone rogue. title: New Update Makes Adding Notes Painfully Slow Since 8.5.0
text:
I’ve been using the Omron app for a long time, and the usability took a major step backward starting with version 8.5.0. The “New Home Screen” update introduced a workflow change that makes adding notes significantly more difficult than before.

Previously, I could add a note directly from the main screen. Now, when I tap a reading, the app takes about 10 seconds to load — and it always loads the chart first. I don’t need the chart, and I don’t use the chart for adding notes, yet I’m forced to see it every single time I want to annotate a reading. After that delay, I have to scroll down to “See all measurements,” but the scrolling is laggy and often requires several swipes before the app responds. Only after selecting “See all measurements” can I scroll again, enable “Show notes,” and finally add a note. This is a clear usability regression.

This change affected me during a medically sensitive moment. I was recently hospitalized for a stroke, and I rely on the ability to quickly annotate readings when symptoms or stress occur. The new slow, chart‑first workflow made it harder to document an important reading in real time, which is unacceptable for a health‑tracking app.

Omron should restore the ability to add notes directly from the main screen or streamline the workflow. Users who depend on this app for real medical situations should not be forced to wait through delays, laggy scrolling, and an unnecessary chart just to record essential information.

If this workflow cannot be improved, I may need to switch to another app that supports my Omron monitor, because quick note‑taking is essential for my medical tracking.

title: UI functionality issue
text:
I like the Caring Bridge app for the most part, but there is one aspect that I find really annoying. If the user is on the main page and is trying to catch up on missed posts, the user simply scrolls down to the oldest post they want to see and opens it. However, when the user then returns to the main page, the main page reverts the user to the top of the main page, so that if the user wants to continue catching up on old posts, the user once again has to scroll down down the page to find where they want to pick up reading. It would be a better user experience if the main page remained in place when the user returns to the main page from reading a post. 

Otherwise, I find CB is o be an excellent way to keep up with the medical journeys of my friends and family members.

title: Inappropriate!

title: Abysmal
text:
We launched our Caringbridge for my father in law. 

Immediately had server issues and couldn’t approve new members. Reached out to support staff and they we refused to help. 

Had over 3000 visitors to the page and couldn’t approve more than 28 individuals to follow. 

Refused to accept responsibility. Stopped responding and never got us a solution.  

I don’t know how to give 0 stars. 1 feels like a lot more than deserved.

title: Need push notifications
text:
Just found this site. It’s great as the one stop shop to keep friends and family up to date.  

That being said.  Having all communications via email is a bit annoying.  As the admin of my wife’s page I am approving requests.   We have a lot of people we are sending the invite link to.  And we want approve requests.  So having to monitor email through out the day is a bit of a pain.   If I could receive push notifications on the phone or text messages. I could respond faster. title: Love this but…
text: I love this app because I can stay connected to my life long friend while she is 4 hours away getting treated for leukemia. We all think it is worse than her parents say. Yesterday they posted go get your update from Caring Bridge and make sure to pray this time. All of my friends and I were really worried. But the app isn’t working. It’s not loading any recent updates. This crushes us, knowing that our life long friend can’t talk to us openly because we don’t know what’s going on. First can you all pray for her while she  does her BEST to fight the leukemia and beat it. Second, can the creators fix this bug? It’s really sad not knowing what’s going on with your friend while she’s in the hospital fighting for her life. Saying all of this this is an AMAZING app 5 out of 5 stars would recommend this is someone you know or love is in the hospital. Not only to know what’s going on but for the most recent updates possible. (Also you can search for anyone) whether that’s a celebrity or someone in your small hometown.

title: Do NOT recommend
text: There are so many glitches with this app. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve typed out a whole post and it gets lost because the app force closes or does not save the draft. Also, they deceivingly advertise “tributes” as a way to directly support the family in need, but instead it is a donation to their own app. I have had several family members think they were donating money to us when in reality it goes to the app. The language must be changed to clarify this distinction. It is disgusting, horrible behavior to pray on people in that manner. This cannot be compliant with standards as a 501(c)(3). We started this page because some folks do not have Facebook or other social media, but we sincerely regret this decision and wished we had just made a Facebook page instead.

title: What happened?
text:
I’ve authored and co-authored several CaringBridge sites over the years. I have appreciated the relative ease of creating, updating and otherwise modifying sites - until earlier this year. Don’t know what happened to blow CaringBridge out of the water a few months ago, and the complete lack of communication about it was baffling. I’d still appreciate something more than “we’re working hard.”

While there’s been progress in recent months, the site still lacks much of its previous usability. As an author, I find it clumsy, difficult, and frustrating to use. More importantly, large numbers of my sister’s supporters and readers have stopped using it, and that is a very great loss.

Are there plans to restore more functionality? Will CaringBridge communicate anything of substance that might help its users? Is anyone paying attention to feedback from the community of users? I hope so.

Thanks for your time and attention.

title: New Format is ZERO Stars…..
text:

My opinion is from a user point of view, not someone with an account - a friend of my family was diagnosed with cancer this year & I have been grateful for this app to follow along to see his progress, & to be able to send messages of prayers & encouragement along the way.

The old format was beautiful, excellent in every way for what it was built to do.  So easy to navigate & read for both posts, updates & comments. It literally felt like when you entered someone’s page, you were walking in a comfortable, sunny room surrounded by friends, family, hope & love. 

This new update could not be more generic if you tried.  It feels stark, cold & cumbersome- literally like you are walking into a cold ICU room-  with absolutely nothing on the walls, surrounded by people you don’t know.  It is truly bad - borderline depressing for me, I can’t imagine how it makes the people who are ill feel.

My only disappointment is that the Emergency Assistance feature isn’t supported in my country. If it were available, I wouldn’t hesitate for a moment to upgrade to the premium plan!

title: Worth the peace and protection
text:
I bought this app years ago and never realized how useful at the time it was going to be for my future.
First my son had his phone stolen on the bus and I went directly to the house to retrieve it back in less than an hour. 

Second, my husband was in another state for work and experienced an accident. The phone didn’t notify me of anything regarding the accident, but when I couldn’t find him I was able to use the Life360 app to tell me where he was and the phone was located inside a hospital. He was brought in as unknown without identification and if it wasn’t for the app putting me in the correct direction it could have been weeks to months or not at all that I was notified about my husband’s whereabouts. Because of the app I was able to find him within a day of him arriving to the hospital and was able to get him started on surgeries he needed.

I’ve kept the app ever since and it’s very reassuring to have for regular day to day.

I would recommend it and I use it daily.

title: Delayed Safety Notifications Defeat the Purpose of Life360
text:
What good is Life360 for parents if notifications that our children have arrived at or departed from a location can be delayed by 3–5 minutes? Parents rely on this app for safety, awareness, and peace of mind. A notification that arrives several minutes after our child has already left or arrived defeats the purpose of receiving that alert in the first place.

When it comes to our children’s safety, timing matters. Parents should not have to wonder whether their child has left school, arrived home, or reached another destination while waiting several minutes for Life360 to notify them.

Life360 needs to take this issue seriously. Location and arrival/departure notifications should be delivered as promptly as technically possible, with reliable background tracking and minimal delays. If there is a technical limitation causing these delays, the company needs to explain it clearly and address it.

Parents depend on this app for more than convenience. We depend on it for information that helps us look after our children. A family safety app should prioritize timely, reliable notifications. Please fix this issue.

The list option helps keep my shopping items available in one place. It also is great to get ready for going to a trip by making a check off list of the things you need to bring with you.

title: Cozi
text:
I absolutely love using Cozi. It has made keeping my family organized so much easier and less stressful. The shared calendar is a game changer—everyone can see what’s going on, and we’re finally not missing appointments or double-booking things anymore.

The grocery lists and to-do lists are also incredibly helpful. Being able to update them in real time and have everyone in the household see the changes instantly just makes everyday life run smoother. It’s simple, easy to use, and actually does what it’s supposed to without being overly complicated.

Overall, Cozi has really helped bring a sense of order to our busy schedule. I’d recommend it to anyone trying to keep their family or household organized.

title: HIGHLY RECOMMEND
text: Cozi is super organized and helpful! I am a type A organizer and my husband is not lol so having this SHARED. Slander and organizer is perfect. Grocery lists we both can see, appointments we both get notifications for. It’s perfect. Thank you Cozi team!!!

title: Convenience

title: Longtime User Frustrated
text: I have had Cozi as my primary calendar app for well over a decade now. Gold member for nearly as long. It got me through the chaos of three kids’ school/activity schedules, countless vacations, managing lists, deadlines, birthdays etc. But I have had more and more glitches with it in the past 6 months where future dates don’t load, or it jumps to some other random date without me even touching the screen. Also, my husband continues to crab that he cannot send me a calendar invitation from his app — which I get, it’s super frustrating now that it’s just our two calendars that we’re coordinating but we can’t. We have followed all the directions to add other calendars to my Cozi account to no avail. I get no notifications.

title: How is it possible to make something exponentially worse?
text: The Fitbit app and user experience were not amazing. But they worked. I was a user for many years and even converted my mom from Apple Watch to Fitbit. With the migration to Google Health, Google truly ruined this product. My understanding is that they fired all their software engineers and had AI create the new app / UX. And it really really shows. title: Still needs major features and fixes
text: I cannot believe that during workout you cannot see your heart rate data. It just shows you your distance. I definitely want to be able to see my heart rate, especially since I got a Fitbit air where I don’t have a screen on the device, I have to rely on my aunt to check my heart rate and my zones. None of that data is available while you’re in a workout. Also, I still cannot get my Fitbit scale to connect to the new Google Health app. And finally, why in the hell does this app not have its own widget? Again, my Fitbit air does not have a screen, and if I wanted to check my steps, I have to open my phone to go all the way to the Google Health app and then look it would be really nice if I had a widget on my lock screen that showed me my steps for the day and my basic health metrics. If honestly, these three features were updated then I would be very happy and upgraded my score to five stars.

title: Algorithm changed - now it's useless
text: I've been a user for years, recently the algorithm changed and it's made the product much less useful. The sleep score in particular is now completely unrelated to sleep quality in any meaningful sense. I will have an awesome night of rest and it will tell me my sleep was terrible - my husband who obviously has sleep apnea will cause earthquakes through the night with his snoring and constantly be waking himself up with it and the algorithm will applaud with tremendous sleep he's just had. Several friends with the product have also noticed that the algorithm around sleep scores in particular was changed and it's made the whole product less useful. If you're not already bought into this product, I recommend trying something else first. I know I'm looking at alternatives.

title: Keeps crashing
text:
We’ve used this app for lists and groceries for years with no issues. For the past ~2 weeks or so, the app crashes more than it works. title: Don’t think, just download it!
text:
This app has been a lifesaver for my family. Yes most of the features are things that come standard on any smartphone, however the convenience of having (almost) everything in one place has helped this busy Dad and Mom get more organized.

We downloaded this initially for the Recipe Box and Meal Planner tools (premium features). Add your favorite recipes to your recipe box, plan your meals, and it automatically adds the ingredients to your list. The amount of time we save each week on meal planning and grocery lists has been well worth the monthly fee!

There are a few features that are lacking and some I’d love to see incorporated.

99% of the time I use the app on my phone and when adding a new task or item to your list, it doesn’t allow you to categorize it until after you have submitted it, sending that to the “uncategorized” section at the bottom of the list. Being able to categorize it when you initially enter the data would save some clicks/time.

Another feature that could use an upgrade is the calendar. It’s nice being able to import your calendar, but integrating it so that you can create an event in the app and have it show up in your default calendar app would be a welcomed update. 

Add some iOS widgets (calendar, notes, todo, shopping list, etc.) 

A wishlist item would be Life360 integration or replacement. The maps is very basic and unreliable. We have noticed inaccuracy in the locations, delayed or non-existent notifications when leaving/arriving at one of our set places. Life360 is an excellent tool for not only location services, but also crash detection, driving summary, and more.

That being said. Don’t think, just download it!

title: Really love this app! Game Changer! A few small suggestions :
text: First suggestion: Is there anyway to snooze specific dates on the calendar that are syncing from the timetable ? For example: My co parent would normally pick up our son on a Tuesday, but this week, he’s out of town at a waterpark. How can I snooze the pick up time that I have syncing from a timetable ? 2nd suggestion: I like that I can sync calendars from other circles. Is there anyway to also sync timetables to other circles ? Or time tables that I have showing up on the calendar to other circles? For example: I am having to input my work schedule twice into each circle. 3rd suggestion: Is there any type of notification option if a calendar between circles gets double booked ? For example: If my immediate household has an event booked on a date that includes specific family members , and the same family member gets booked on the same date and time on a calendar in a different circle, if it can notify the user & or founder , that they’re double booked. 4th suggestion: Can I just import contacts from my phone contacts instead of having to add them in manually? Otherwise - I can already tell that this app is going to be a life saver !! So thankful I found it ! Thank you for helping keep families sane !!!

title: This app is amazing!
text:
As a full time working + busy mom of 4, this app has given me so much organization in my life! I previously utilized many of these features amongst numerous apps - so this is amazing to have everything together. I LOVE that my entire family can see our calendar and lists and they can contribute to everything in real time. I have already convinced other family members and co-workers to join! 

I have two improvement suggestions. In the Contact Book, it would be nice to have a notes/free text section when adding in more fields. I have additional details I’d like to write down for my family to access should they need it. Secondly, I love the Timetable feature, but I wish it didn’t automatically open directly into one of them. I have numerous tables for each of my children and I would like to select which one I’d like to open - similar to the way the tiles look on the home screen. 

Thanks again for an amazing app!!

title: Task editing/creation needs improvement
text: Overall this is a really cool app with so much potential to help my family be organized but the limited functionality of the task entry interface in lists prevents me from using this. If you edit a task the category to which it was assigned changes to uncategorized from whatever category you had originally tagged the task. It is a pain to recategorize because you have to click a separate button on the app or web interface to categorize a task. If the developer could make two changes this problem would be eliminated: (1) stop changing a task to “uncategorized” just because the name/title of the task is changed and (2) create a task entry interface that allows the user to (a) categorize the task at the same time that the task is created and (b) select the status of the task (undone, done, in progress, on hold) in the same interface with which the task is created (right now you have to create a task in a little field, then once the task is created you have to click another button to assign a category to the task, then click save, and click a third button to mark complete — all of this should be able to be in one interface, even if there remains a “quick add” field for adding uncategorized tasks). Hopefully the developer can add this functionality and this app would be great!
